v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.en: Let us adore God * Our Saviour.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.la: Deus, ne síleas a me, remítte mihi.
v.en: O Lord, be not thou silent, forgive me.

r.la: Quóniam íncola ego sum apud te et peregrínus.
r.en: For I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner.

text.en: Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.

text.la: Restítue ánimam meam * a malefáctis eórum, Dómine.
text.en: Rescue, O Lord, * my soul from their malice.

text.la: Exsúrge, Dómine, * et inténde iudício meo.
text.en: Arise, O Lord, * and be attentive to my judgment.

text.la: Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
text.en: Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

text.la: Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem iustos Dóminus.
text.en: The arms of the wicked * shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.

text.la: Ne in ira tua * corrípias me, Dómine.
text.en: O Lord, * do not chastise me in thy wrath.

text.la: Inténde in adiutórium meum, * Dómine, virtus salútis meæ.
text.en: Attend unto my help, * O Lord, the God of my salvation.

text.la: Ámove, Dómine, * a me plagas tuas.
text.en: Remove, O Lord, * thy scourges from me.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
text.en: May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

benedictio.la: Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
benedictio.en: May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.

source.en: Lesson from the second letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

text.la: 1 Scimus enim quóniam, si terréstris domus nostra huius habitatiónis dissolvátur, quod ædificatiónem ex Deo habémus, domum non manufáctam, ætérnam in cælis. 2 Nam et in hoc ingemíscimus, habitatiónem nostram, quæ de cælo est, superíndui cupiéntes: 3 Si tamen vestíti, non nudi inveniámur. 4 Nam et qui sumus in hoc tabernáculo, ingemíscimus graváti: eo quod nólumus exspoliári, sed supervestíri, ut absorbeátur quod mortále est, a vita.
text.en: 1 For we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven. 2 For in this also we groan, desiring to be clothed upon with our habitation that is from heaven. 3 Yet so that we be found clothed, not naked. 4 For we also, who are in this tabernacle, do groan, being burthened; because we would not be unclothed, but clothed upon, that that which is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

body.la: Auribus pércipe, Deus, lácrimas meas: ne síleas a me, remítte mihi:
body.en: O God, give ear unto my tears; hold not thy peace, but, O, spare me!

refrain.la: Quóniam íncola ego sum apud te, et peregrínus.
refrain.en: For I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner.

verse.la: Compláceat tibi, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
verse.en: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me; O Lord, look upon me to help me.

text.la: per fidem enim ambulámus, et non per spéciem
text.en: For we walk by faith, and not by sight.

benedictio.la: Christus perpétuæ det nobis gáudia vitæ.
benedictio.en: May Christ to all His people give, for ever in His sight to live.

text.la: 6 Audéntes ígitur semper, sciéntes, quóniam dum sumus in córpore, peregrinámur a Dómino: 7 8 Audémus autem, et bonam voluntátem habémus magis peregrinári a córpore, et præséntes esse ad Dóminum. 9 Et ídeo conténdimus sive abséntes, sive præséntes, placére illi. 10 Omnes enim nos manifestári opórtet ante tribúnal Christi, ut réferat unusquísque própria córporis, prout gessit, sive bonum, sive malum.
text.en: 6 Therefore having always confidence, knowing that, while we are in the body, we are absent from the Lord. 7 8 But we are confident, and have a good will to be absent rather from the body, and to be present with the Lord. 9 And therefore we labour, whether absent or present, to please him. 10 For we must all be manifested before the judgement seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he hath done, whether it be good or evil.

body.la: Státuit Dóminus supra petram pedes meos, et diréxit gressus meos Deus:
body.en: The Lord hath set my feet upon a rock, and ordered my goings.

refrain.la: Et misit in os meum cánticum novum.
refrain.en: And He hath put a new song in my mouth.

verse.la: Exaudívit preces meas: et edúxit me de lacu misériæ.
verse.en: He heard my cry He brought me up also out of an horrible pit.

benedictio.la: Ignem sui amóris accéndat Deus in córdibus nostris.
benedictio.en: May the Spirit's fire Divine in our hearts enkindled shine.

text.la: 11 Sciéntes ergo timórem Dómini homínibus suadémus, Deo autem manifésti sumus. Spero autem et in consciéntiis vestris maniféstos nos esse. 12 Non íterum commendámus nos vobis, sed occasiónem damus vobis gloriándi pro nobis: ut habeátis ad eos qui in fácie gloriántur, et non in corde. 13 Sive enim mente excédimus, Deo: sive sóbrii sumus, vobis. 14 Cáritas enim Christi urget nos: æstimántes hoc, quóniam si unus pro ómnibus mórtuus est, ergo omnes mórtui sunt: 15 Et pro ómnibus mórtuus est Christus: ut et qui vivunt, iam non sibi vivant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mórtuus est et resurréxit.
text.en: 11 Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we use persuasion to men; but to God we are manifest. And I trust also that in your consciences we are manifest. 12 We commend not ourselves again to you, but give you occasion to glory in our behalf; that you may have somewhat to answer them who glory in face, and not in heart. 13 For whether we be transported in mind, it is to God; or whether we be sober, it is for you. 14 For the charity of Christ presseth us: judging this, that if one died for all, then all were dead. 15 And Christ died for all; that they also who live, may not now live to themselves, but unto him who died for them, and rose again.

body.en: I said: Lord, be merciful unto me.

refrain.la: Sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
refrain.en: Heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui cæléstia simul et terréna moderáris: supplicatiónes pópuli tui cleménter exáudi; et pacem tuam nostris concéde tempóribus.
text.en: Almighty and eternal God, as thou govern all things in heaven and on earth; in thy mercy hear the supplication of thy people, and grant thy peace in our times.

office.title: Feria III infra Hebd II post Epiphaniam
